pf.license.renewals: optional reminders the owner sets; a license the owner says has lapsed pauses that person's new bookings for that work (the owner's word, never a check)
pf.license.insurance: malpractice insurance where the state's form asks for it

pf.money.before: nothing taken at booking when a plan pays; a card saved only where the clinic turns on its late-cancel fee, keeps a card on file for the share, or for a video session; at home, a card saved for a self-pay family
pf.money.plans: the plans the practice takes (its own list); the front desk checks each plan by hand and records it: active or not, the copay, any deductible left, whether the plan must OK the sessions, and any yearly visit limit; the family's share is an estimate, not a promise
pf.money.approvals: where a plan must OK the sessions, the desk asks after the evaluation and records the sessions OK'd, used and left, and the end date; Rosie warns the desk before they run out and never contacts the plan
pf.money.visitLimit: a plan's yearly limit on therapy visits is counted for a weekly plan; the desk is warned before it runs out and tells the family the self-pay price in time
pf.money.selfPay: self-pay families pay the price list (the example clinic: $140 for an evaluation, $110 a session) at each visit; they're told while booking that they can get a written price estimate, and get it on time; a bill far above it can be disputed (the federal rules set how)
pf.money.outOfNetwork: where the practice doesn't take the family's plan, the family pays the self-pay price at each visit and gets a receipt on the secure page with what its plan asks for, to send to the plan itself; the practice never promises what the plan pays back
pf.money.fees: the late-cancel or missed-visit fee: $20 at the example clinic, free to cancel until 24 hours before; $89 for a self-pay home visit, free to cancel until 7am on the day; only with a card saved and the family's yes to those words when booking, and only when the owner confirms each one
pf.money.feeFree: a switch from the state's and the plan's rules: no fee ever for families a plan or the rules protect (like Medicaid, where that applies); for some plans, only if every client pays the same fee; the owner can mark any family fee-free, and names reasons that never carry a fee, like a sick child; their texts say 'No fee to cancel or miss'
pf.money.after: the share at the front desk at each visit, the clinic's own way, or the saved card charged at DONE where the clinic keeps a card on file (and for video sessions); a balance after the plan pays is the practice's own bill, never Rosie's text; home visits: the office bills the plan its own way, and a self-pay visit is charged to the saved card at DONE
pf.money.video: where the family's plan doesn't pay for video sessions, a session is offered at the clinic, or self-pay (a switch from the plan's rules)
pf.money.weeklyPlan: a weekly plan's sessions are each paid when they happen, like a single visit: nothing paid ahead and no monthly charge
pf.money.rosfield: the $2 per booking applies to this work, as to every kind of work (D97): a flat fee for each booking Rosie's AI makes, shown at sign-up for the owner's yes; a booking the business puts in itself carries no $2; card payments cost only Stripe's own card fee, paid to Stripe
pf.money.caps: fee limits for plan patients: from the plan's and the state's rules
pf.money.packages: where a clinic sells self-pay session packs, it sells them at the clinic only, never while booking; a booking can use a session from one; prepaid sessions follow the state's rules on prepaid care (a written cancel period, a refund of unused sessions): a switch
pf.money.repeatPlans: a check-in session every 4 weeks is paid when it happens, like a single visit; nothing paid ahead
pf.money.publicPrograms: early intervention and school services are paid by those programs and are never booked here

pf.messages.staffReasons: families never hear why a therapist is out

pf.staff.oks: the owner OKs same-day times, feeding or swallowing evaluations, any custom price (at the clinic, every one; at home, over $500), and anything a therapist flags
pf.staff.standIn: an evaluation or a re-check: only another speech therapist; a session: a speech therapist, or an assistant under the same plan; a video session: only someone licensed where the client is; the plug-in turns Rosie's no-reply default off: nobody, and never a child, is moved to another therapist without the family's yes
pf.staff.desk: Pat, the office manager, runs the desk: plan checks, referrals, forms and estimates

pf.rules.records: therapy records are kept by the practice for as long as the state's rules require (a child's records may be kept longer); a delete request removes only Rosie's own booking details, never the practice's records
pf.rules.copies: a client's or parent's copy of the records within the time the rules set; Rosie sends only booking and payment records
pf.rules.referral: a switch from the state's form and the plan: whether a doctor's referral or prescription is needed before therapy; the office tracks it
pf.rules.planOfCare: where a plan asks for it, the doctor signs the plan of care; the practice tracks the signature
pf.rules.showLicense: the license shown where the state asks: posted at the clinic, and on a home visit
pf.rules.minors: who may consent for a minor, and at what age a minor may consent alone (a switch from the state form)
pf.rules.schools: school plan services belong to the school district; private therapy alongside them is the parent's choice
pf.rules.estimate: a written price estimate for self-pay families, on the timing the federal rules set
pf.rules.ads: no free-visit or price claims the state's rules don't allow
pf.rules.privacy: health privacy rules for every message and form
pf.rules.homeSales: a switch from the state's form: a written right to cancel care sold at a home visit but not yet given, like a pack of sessions paid ahead, where the state's rules give one; care already given at the visit, like a mealtime visit done that day, has no cancel period, and neither does the booked visit

pf.edges.standIn: a therapist out: another speech therapist for an evaluation, with the family's yes, or new times with no fee; families never hear why
pf.edges.crossState: a family across a state line from the clinic: a video session only with a therapist licensed in the family's state; otherwise a clinic visit
pf.edges.hearing: a hearing screening not passed: the therapist refers the child to an audiologist; sessions can still start
pf.edges.parentSteps: a parent who must step out during a child's session: the session pauses until the parent or a named adult is back
pf.edges.forms: a form not done by its due date: one reminder, then Sam keeps the visit (signed on the secure page before any work), moves it, or cancels with no fee (A7-74, B7-61)
pf.edges.planChange: the plan check comes back not covered: self-pay, or a free cancel
pf.edges.approvalRunsOut: the plan's OK'd sessions or its yearly limit are about to run out: the desk is warned before the last one, and asks for more or tells the family the self-pay price
pf.edges.twoBookings: a parent with two children booked, or a weekly plan: Rosie asks which booking before any change
pf.edges.healthQuestion: a question about a child's speech, eating or progress goes to the therapist; Rosie gives no advice
pf.edges.urgent: no service is sent now and nobody is on call: the soonest time shows first, with the owner's OK for same day; the stroke and choking words get 911

Why: a speech practice runs like it: an evaluation by a licensed therapist, then a plan of care with a weekly series booked by the client's own yes, plans checked by hand, video sessions only where the therapist is licensed for where the client is, home visits on the other side, and no $2 for a health practice. What it lacked came from the pediatrician overlay: a parent or guardian books for a child, who may bring the child is a switch, and children's details stay on the secure page.
Names: Sam Lee, a speech therapist, owns Lee Home Speech (the master's main company: home speech therapy and hearing care, 520 Main St, a 25-mile area) and Lee Speech Therapy (the second company: the clinic, 30 Cedar Ave). Flow A's story is at the clinic: Alex's daughter Lily, 4. Flow B's is at the family's home, 9 Aspen Ln: Alex's son Max, 2.
People: at the clinic, Iris (speech therapist; Spanish; feeding work; the clinic's home visits) and Elise (speech therapist, Saturday afternoons). On the home team, Caleb (speech therapist, also a licensed audiologist, feeding work) and Tia (speech therapy assistant, sessions only, under a therapist's plan). Sam, Pat and Alex M. stay. The pilot's people are all renamed; other clients keep master names (Dee W., Ben T., Nia K., Lin W., Morgan P., Kim L.) or new ones (Nora S., Ruth P., Ivy C.).
Kinds of work: plumbing became home speech therapy, electrical became hearing care (it waits for its audiologist's license), the barbershop became the clinic. Licenses are switches from the state's form: each speech therapist's own license (Sam's SP045210), an assistant's or a clinical fellow's credential where the state asks, an audiologist's license for hearing care, and the practice's registration (PR20981) only where asked.
Who books: a parent or legal guardian for anyone under 18 (Rosie's rule for this work until a state's form says otherwise; the minor-consent age is a switch); an adult for themselves; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent, like after a stroke (Rosa for her mother). Anyone else is asked to have a parent book. Who may bring the child is a switch: a parent, or an adult the parent OKs on the secure page (A8-02, A8-51 to A8-60, B4-26, B4-27). At a preschool session, the parent signs an OK and stays reachable by phone (S1-59, B4-66).
Privacy: the AI hears only the kind of visit, the child's age, the languages at home, a school plan yes or no, a referral yes or not yet, and the plan's name. The child's name, birth date, the reason, test results and health history go only on the secure page. Customer texts carry the business, date, time and place, never the child's name or the visit type; an extra service in a text is 'one more thing' or 'the extra visit', with what it is on the secure page. Owner and staff texts use initials (L.M., M.M. for the child; A.M. for the parent) and a link. At home the therapist's name stays, for the door check.
Safety: stroke signs at any age (sudden trouble speaking, a drooping face, weakness on one side), choking now or trouble breathing get 'Call 911 now' and no booking; self-harm words get 988 and 911. Coughing at meals with no choking now gets the 911 words first, then the booking goes on (A3-23, B3-18, B7-17). Rosie never judges how serious anything is.
Prices are the example practices' own, not a standard: clinic evaluation $140 (75 min), session $110 (45 min), re-check $120, adult evaluation $140, voice check $40 (the one recording room), feeding evaluation $160 with Sam's OK, hearing screening $20 added to an evaluation, video session $110, a plan's $35 copay, a $20 late-cancel or missed-visit fee only where Sam turns it on. Home: evaluation $179 (75 min), session $150, mealtime visit $160, adult evaluation at home $199 ($249 with Sam), an $89 fee for self-pay visits only. Hearing care: $60 hearing test, $20 ear check, preschool screenings $120 an hour.
Money A: list|none|counter is the main path: nothing taken; the desk checks the plan by hand; the copay at the front desk at each visit; self-pay families pay the list price there, and a family whose plan the clinic doesn't take gets a receipt to send its plan (A9-03, A9-20, A8-x04). list|card|counter: the clinic's $20 late-cancel fee, free to cancel until 24 hours before, a card saved for it, Sam confirms each charge, never for a fee-free family. list|card|card: Saturday mornings with no front desk, and video sessions: the card is charged at DONE. Left out: holds, deposits and full price (therapy is never paid ahead), photos and visit pricing (every service is on the list), Rosie's texted bill (the clinic has a front desk).
Money B: list|none|own is the main path (the office bills the family's plan its own way). list|card|card is self-pay: a card saved, $179 charged at DONE, and an $89 fee after 7am on the day only if Sam confirms it. A self-pay family hears about the written price estimate before saying yes (B4-28). Left out: holds, deposits, full price, a texted bill, photos and visit pricing.
Sign-up words follow that (S1-12 to S1-18, S1-41 to S1-47): plan families book with nothing taken; self-pay home families save a card; the clinic saves a card only for its fee or a Saturday-morning visit. No tips, no bank transfer, no $2 (S1-26, S1-62, S1-65).
Referral: a switch from the state's form (A4-x01 to A4-x03, B4-x01 to B4-x03): not needed to evaluate (the story); allowed with limits (marked 'no referral', only therapists the state allows, the desk counts the limit); needed first (nothing booked). Where the plan wants one before weekly sessions, the office asks the child's doctor itself with the parent's OK (A4-48, B4-42), and the sessions wait for it.
Public programs: said once, as information (Rosie's rule): a child 3 or older can get a free evaluation from the school district (A4-50); under 3, the state's early intervention program (B4-05). Speech services in a school plan are never booked: the school district gives them (A4-38).
Own steps: A8-x09 and A8-x10, a pass-or-fail hearing screening when Alex adds it (refer to an audiologist if not passed; sessions can still start). After the evaluation, Iris sets the plan of care (A8-x01), the desk records the plan's OK (A8-x02: 12 sessions until Fri Jan 29; pending; or self-pay), and the weekly plan goes out for Alex's own yes (A8-x05 to A8-x08: Tuesdays 3:30pm, after preschool). Flow B does the same for 12 weekly home sessions, mostly with Tia under Caleb's plan (B8-x01 to B8-x05). A10-x01 and A10-x02: a progress check at the 6th session, and a desk warning before the plan's OK or its yearly visit limit runs out.
Video: a session (never a first child evaluation, the example clinic's rule) only with a therapist licensed where the child is during the session, or with a compact privilege the state's form allows; a family across a state line from the clinic gets only therapists licensed in its state, or a clinic time (A4-36, A8-03).
Flow B books a set start time (B4-83 keeps '2 A set start time'; arrival windows are off): a toddler's home session starts at 9:00am, not in a window. The master's window words are renamed to start times in B.
Stand-ins: nobody is moved to another therapist without the family's yes, so Sam turns the no-reply default off (A7-21, B7-20, B7-22, S11-46, S11-49), as the pediatrician overlay does. Families never hear why a therapist is out.
A sick child never means a fee: Sam's own rule (A7-13, A8-14, pf.edges.sickChild). Fee-free families (Medicaid where that applies) are a switch in pf.money.
Off, beyond the pilot's: in B, weather (indoor work) and arrival windows. splitsKept: A7-61 (Elise may stand in for an evaluation; nobody else for feeding work) and A8-02 (all here, or something missing).
